ai.title: Add Context7 documentation fetching to agent prompt
ai.summary: New backend integration fetches relevant documentation chunks from Context7 based on user queries. Uses Gemini to analyze query relevance and select optimal project/topic. Injects retrieved context directly into main agent prompt as user message. Covers backend API client and prompt assembly logic.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant a coding question, it now automatically pulls in relevant documentation from Context7 and tucks it into the prompt it sends to the model. That means the assistant starts answering with the official docs already in hand, instead of trying to recall everything from its own training. You'd notice when you ask something like 'How do I use React hooks?' the assistant can reference specific, recent documentation snippets directly in its reply, because the background integration fetches and injects those pieces before the conversation even reaches the model.

ai.title: ts-ignore for bun:test import
ai.summary: Added @ts-ignore directive to bun:test import in background-process-manager.test.ts. Suppresses TypeScript type-checking errors for the test module. Internal change affecting npm-app test suite only.

eli5.text: The test suite that checks the app's internal task-running code had a small behind-the-scenes adjustment: one line was added to tell the type-checker to ignore a note about the testing tool it uses. If you looked at the test files, you'd see a comment added before the import of the testing library, but otherwise nothing about how the app actually runs for you has changed. This is purely maintenance inside the project's own tests and is already in place.

ai.title: Update main-prompt tests for async generator mocks
ai.summary: Replaced ReadableStream mocks with async generator implementations in main-prompt.test.ts. Updated streamGemini25ProWithFallbacks, promptClaudeStream, and promptGeminiStream mocks to yield strings directly. Scope limited to backend/src/__tests__/main-prompt.test.ts.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the team updated how they simulate the assistant's streaming responses during automated checks. Rather than faking those responses with one kind of mock object, they switched to a simpler, more direct approach. Nothing changes for you as a user - these checks just run faster and more reliably now.

ai.title: Skip slow rewrite tests
ai.summary: Marked `preserveCommentsInEditSnippet` and `rewriteWithOpenAI` test suites as skipped in `backend/src/__tests__/fast-rewrite.test.ts`. Change addresses slow execution times for these specific integration tests. Scope limited to backend test configuration; no production code or user-facing features affected. Tests remain in codebase but excluded from default run.

eli5.text: The team turned off two of their slowest automated checks so the rest of the testing process finishes faster, and you would only notice if you were watching the test results: those two specific checks no longer run by default. The code that actually powers the product is completely untouched, so no one using the tool experiences anything different; only developers working on the code see speedier test feedback.

ai.title: Refine docs search prompt constraints
ai.summary: Updated the JSON schema instruction in `get-documentation-for-query.ts` to explicitly restrict `topic` field generation to relevant documentation keywords only. This change tightens the prompt to reduce noise in search queries by enforcing stricter relevance criteria during LLM extraction. Scope limited to backend documentation retrieval logic.

eli5.text: The system that finds relevant documentation based on your questions now does a better job of ignoring unrelated keywords when searching, so the answers you get back are more on target. This behind-the-scenes adjustment tightens how the search decides which topics are worth including, reducing noise in the results. It's already live and affects anyone relying on the assistant to pull up accurate documentation.

ai.title: Fix type error in background-process-manager tests
ai.summary: Split `bun:test` imports in `background-process-manager.test.ts` into separate statements with targeted `@ts-ignore` comments. Replaces a single block ignoring all types with granular suppression for the test runner types. Scope limited to `npm-app` test utilities.

eli5.text: The testing setup for the app's background job monitoring was telling the code-checking tool to ignore type errors for the entire block of test imports, which is too broad. It now splits those imports into two smaller groups, each with its own targeted note explaining that the test framework's special instructions aren't recognized by the regular code checker. This only affects the internal test code that verifies the background monitoring works correctly, and it cleans up the test utilities so they follow better practices. Nothing users see has changed.

ai.title: Fix logger splitter
ai.summary: Rewrote backend/src/util/logger.ts splitData function to handle nested objects and arrays correctly. Previous implementation failed on complex structures due to naive string slicing and incorrect overhead calculation. New logic recursively splits plain objects and arrays while respecting JSON serialization limits and key overheads. Updated tests in backend/src/util/__tests__/logger.test.ts cover edge cases for large strings and deep nesting.

eli5.text: When the system logs large pieces of data, it now correctly breaks them into smaller chunks that fit within the size limits, instead of failing or producing unreadable errors when the data is too complex. Previously, deeply nested objects or very large text values would cause logging to break; the logging process would choke on structures that contained other structures or arrays. Now the system carefully splits these complex data shapes into multiple readable log entries while respecting the size limit, so you will see complete, well-formed log lines instead of truncated or broken ones when inspecting logs that contain large or nested data.

ai.title: Revert main prompt user instructions to pre-Gemini rewrite
ai.summary: Reverted the user instructions section in backend/src/main-prompt.ts to its pre-Gemini rewrite state. The previous version contained extensive bold markdown, nested bullet points, and explicit override/supersede logic that likely caused formatting or adherence issues. The new version uses plain text paragraphs, simplified tool formatting rules (no XML attributes), and direct instructions for clarification, file reading, subgoals, and code preservation. Scope limited to the backend main prompt construction.

eli5.text: The assistant's instructions were simplified back to a cleaner, less formatted version. You would notice the difference if you compared the prompt structure, it now reads as plain paragraphs instead of heavily styled bullet points and bold text. This change only affects the backend prompt construction and was made on April 12, 2025.

ai.title: browseraction tool enables headless console log reading
ai.summary: Adds `browser_action` tool for navigating URLs and capturing console logs in headless mode. Default `headless` set to `true` in `BROWSER_DEFAULTS`. Pre/post screenshots and 'Browser started' log disabled in `browser-runner.ts`. Handler returns JSON string instead of object.

eli5.text: The assistant can now open a web page in a hidden browser and read the console logs that websites print out, which helps it spot errors or debug problems on a live site. Previously, the browser would open in a visible window and take extra screenshots that cluttered the process; now it runs quietly in the background by default and skips those screenshots. When something goes wrong, instead of returning a raw error object, the assistant now hands back a clean JSON string summarizing the failure so the result is easier to parse. This feature is live today for anyone using the assistant to inspect web applications they're actively developing.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.215
ai.summary: Incremented `codebuff` package version from 1.0.214 to 1.0.215. No functional changes or new features included in this release. Update limited to `npm-app/package.json`.

eli5.text: If you use the AI coding assistant, updating to this release lets it pull in relevant technical documentation automatically while it works, and it lets you navigate to a web address and silently capture what shows up in the browser's console log. It also keeps the background tasks from flooding your terminal with endless error text, and makes the local logging quieter when you're running things on your own machine for testing. The version number itself is just a label that lets package managers find and install the latest copy.

ai.title: Add /vibe redirect for referral link
ai.summary: Added a new redirect rule in web/next.config.mjs mapping /vibe to the codebuff.com referral URL. This provides a shorter, easier-to-share link for users. The redirect is configured as non-permanent.

eli5.text: Visiting the web address /vibe on the company website now instantly takes you to a special referral link for Codebuff. This is a behind-the-scenes addition to the website's settings, and it works right now the moment someone types or clicks that short path.

ai.title: Referral bonus raised to 500 credits
ai.summary: CREDITS_REFERRAL_BONUS increased from 250 to 500 in common/src/constants.ts. Adjusts incentive value for user referrals. Change scoped to shared core constants. Existing affiliate limits (AFFILIATE_USER_REFFERAL_LIMIT = 500) remain unchanged.

eli5.text: Starting today, anyone who refers a friend to the service now earns 500 credits instead of the previous 250 when that friend signs up. This doubles the reward you get for sharing the referral link, while the separate cap on how many referrals you can make still stays at 500. You'd notice the higher payout the next time you refer someone and their bonus lands in your account.

ai.title: Refactor splitData into dedicated util module
ai.summary: Extracted `splitData` logic from `backend/src/util/logger.ts` into new `backend/src/util/split-data.ts`. Implements robust chunking for plain objects and strings, calculating JSON size overhead and handling edge cases like empty strings and oversized keys. `logger.ts` now imports from the new module, reducing inline complexity. Covers backend core utilities; no user-facing API or model changes.

eli5.text: The system that records what happens inside the app now uses a separate, more careful helper for breaking up large pieces of information before writing them down. You won't see this when you use the app, it only changes how the program stores its own logs behind the scenes, but it should now handle big messages more reliably without choking on things like empty text or unusually long single words.

ai.title: Remove knowledge file creation condition
ai.summary: The condition `hasKnowledgeFiles` was removed from the prompt instruction for updating knowledge files in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. This allows the agent to consider creating new knowledge files even when none currently exist, provided it is not the first user message.

eli5.text: The assistant can now be reminded to save useful notes it learns during a conversation, even if it has not saved any notes before, as long as it is not your very first message to it. Previously, this reminder only appeared when both conditions were true (it already had notes and it was not the first message); now it only needs the second condition, so the prompt that nudges it to record new notes fires more often. You would notice this only if you happened to inspect how the assistant is being instructed behind the scenes; most users will not see anything different in their chats.

ai.title: Background process updates sent every prompt action
ai.summary: Refactors background process reporting in `npm-app` to send updates on every prompt action rather than only on user prompts. `getBackgroundProcessUpdates` in `background-process-manager.ts` now returns a structured `ToolResult` or `null`, integrating directly with the agent state. `client.ts` appends these updates to `toolResults` during the non-complete prompt loop, ensuring real-time status visibility for long-running tasks.

eli5.text: As you work on a long-running task, you will now see status updates from background work appear in real time with each assistant turn instead of only when you type a new message. Previously, progress from background processes was only reported at the start of your next prompt, which could leave you waiting without knowing what was happening. The system now checks for and shows these updates automatically during every step of the task, giving you a clearer picture of ongoing work. This is a behind-the-scenes improvement to how status information is gathered and displayed during tasks.
